To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there was little improvement in the domain boundary prediction and contact prediction categories.

1) The CASP8 domain boundary prediction category demonstrated that the predictors continue to struggle with the prediction of domain boundaries for the few abinitio targets in CASPs, despite a large number of predictors participating in this category; 2) The CASP 8 contact prediction category demonstrated an increase in the prediction accuracy, with the contact specialists predicting contacts more accurately than majority of tertiary structure prediction methods.
the domain boundary prediction methods still make reasonable predictions for targets that are related to templates, but continue not to make good predictions of ab initio targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the study of protein structure.
the study of the structure, function, dynamics and interactions of proteins, and the development of computational methods to predict their structure, function, and interactions.
the development of methods for the analysis of the spatial distribution of protein residues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the domain prediction category continues to struggle to make accurate predictions and that the contact prediction category has improved in accuracy but is still a long way from being useful for protein structure modeling.
the domain boundary prediction methods continue to make reliable predictions for those targets with structural templates, but still struggle with the few ab inito targets.
the CASP experiment is a valuable tool for the assessment of protein structure prediction methods, but that the assessment of domain prediction is not as useful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have made some progress in the domain prediction area, but that we have not yet solved the problem.

the domain prediction category continues to be of limited value to the field of structural bioinformatics and contact prediction is a useful category but one that is difficult to assess due to the lack of free‐modeling targets.
the domain prediction category is still a challenge, but the contact prediction category is showing promise and is likely to return in a modified form in future CASP experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are still not able to reliably predict domain boundaries in proteins, and that we are still unable to reliably predict contacts in proteins, especially for ab initio targets.
there is little evidence that domain boundary prediction is improving.
there was no significant improvement over the last few CASP experiments.
